Industrial intelligence begins with a practical question: can an AI agent turn operational evidence into a reliable next step?

AssetOpsBench brings that question into a reproducible environment. It connects sensor observations, failure knowledge, time-series analysis, and maintenance workflows so researchers and practitioners can build agents, inspect their decisions, and evaluate their performance. The research benchmark includes 141 expert-curated scenarios, with 99 single-agent tasks and 42 tasks requiring multiple agents. Read the benchmark study →

Quick Start

git clone https://github.com/IBM/AssetOpsBench.git
cd AssetOpsBench
pip install -e .

Follow INSTRUCTIONS.md to configure services and run a documented agent workflow. You can also explore the Hugging Face playground or the Colab notebook.

Active development is on main. Publication-specific code is maintained on branches including IndustryAssetEQA and main-0.x.

From operational evidence to evaluated action

The current repository exposes five domain MCP servers—IoT, failure modes, time-series analysis, work orders, and vibration—plus shared utilities. Its agent implementations include Plan Execute, Deep Agent, Claude Agent, OpenAI Agent, Stirrup, and OpenCode. Explore their interfaces and configuration in the repository and server documentation.

Together, these components support a research workflow:

  1. Choose a task grounded in asset operations.
  2. Connect the evidence through domain tools and data interfaces.
  3. Run an agent or pipeline and record its trajectory.
  4. Evaluate the result against the scenario's expected behavior.
  5. Investigate failures and share improvements others can reproduce.

The KDD hands-on tutorial walks through this process, from MCP tools to a grounded work-order agent and an auditable leaderboard.

A family of industrial AI benchmarks

AssetOpsBench connects complementary research questions across industrial operations. Each benchmark has its own task, release, and evaluation protocol.

Benchmark The question it asks Explore
AssetOpsBench Can agents coordinate tools and evidence to complete industrial operations tasks? Paper · Data
FailureSensorIQ Can models reason about relationships between failure modes and sensors? Paper · Data
DiagnosticIQ Given a triggered symbolic rule, can a model recommend the appropriate maintenance action? Paper · Data on Kaggle
PHMForge Can agents select and sequence algorithm-grounded tools for prognostics and health management? Paper · Data and datasheet
IoTBench / ReActXen Can language agents retrieve the right industrial sensor data? Published study
IndustryAssetEQA Can industrial explanations be grounded in telemetry and failure knowledge? Published study

DiagnosticIQ comprises 6,690 multiple-choice questions derived from 118 expert-authored rule–action pairs across 16 asset types. Its five variants probe distractor pressure, surface changes, prose formulations, condition inversion, and rationales. The October 2026 paper evaluates 29 LLMs and four embedding baselines. DiagnosticIQ v2

PHMForge pairs 99 scenarios across eight asset classes with 39 MCP-native tools in the August 2026 paper. The current dataset card provides separate rotating/aero and lithium-ion configurations and documents overlap with the AssetOpsBench PHM release, so their counts should not be added as independent tasks. PHMForge paper · Dataset card

PHMForge on Harbor: 123 packaged tasks adapt the 99 scenarios for general-purpose agents working from data. This setup omits PHMForge’s MCP servers; its scores are separate from the paper’s evaluation. Package details

The team has announced NeurIPS 2026 acceptance for DiagnosticIQ and PHMForge; PHMForge's dataset card identifies the Evaluations & Datasets track. These are acceptance announcements, distinct from records of conference presentations already delivered.

Learn by building

Explore the AAAI 2027 lab. The time-series scientific-discovery lab introduces TSM-MCP-Kit, an sktime-backed MCP server, through evidence inspection, recipe composition, diagnostic refinement, evaluation, and search. Lab materials are being released in stages; consult the site for availability.

Start with a guided lab. The KDD tutorial covers environment setup, industrial MCP tools, agent execution, and evaluation.

Explore the underlying techniques. Study the ReActXen IoT agent tutorial, FailureSensorIQ evaluation code, and AssetOpsBench technical material.

Connect research to implementation. Follow the setup instructions, select a documented pipeline, and retain its configuration alongside your results.

Find the comparison that matches your question. Model knowledge, agent execution, and competition rankings measure different capabilities.

Comparison What it measures Explore
Kaggle AssetOpsBench leaderboard The page currently describes FailureSensorIQ multiple-choice evaluation across 10 industrial asset types; broader agentic evaluation is described as future work Leaderboard and scope
DiagnosticIQ research leaderboard Maintenance-action recommendation and variant robustness; published tables rather than a verified standalone live service Paper and score definitions

CODS competition rankings Submitted systems evaluated in planning and execution tracks, including public and hidden evaluation Codabench competition · Results analysis
Reproducible tutorial leaderboard Agent outputs evaluated against static scenario data in a guided workflow KDD tutorial · Evaluation documentation

Read scores alongside the dataset revision, model configuration, track, and scoring protocol. The CODS retrospective shows why: public scores and hidden execution scores had a correlation of −0.13 in its analyzed sample, and changing the scaling of one composite-score term would exchange the top two teams. A ranking is meaningful only with its measurement context.

Competitions

Build an agent. Test it under shared conditions. Learn from the failures. Public challenges turn the ecosystem into a place to experiment, compare approaches, and contribute reproducible evidence.

CODS 2025 · AssetOpsBench-Live

The challenge invited teams to develop industrial agents across sensing, reasoning, and action, including maintenance diagnosis and work-order tasks. Its planning and execution tracks are analyzed in the subsequent retrospective. Official conference challenge page · Codabench platform

The official schedule listed a November 13, 2025 submission deadline and December 20 award ceremony. The later retrospective examines a specific 300-attempt server log and 149 registered teams. These scoped counts should be kept distinct from broader participation totals reported in other project publications.

IJCAI 2026 · Industrial Automation Challenge

Hosted on Kaggle by the organizing team, the challenge explores physics-grounded industrial reasoning. Track 1 evaluates internal model reasoning in a closed-book setting, with maintenance and failure-analysis questions. Its listed submission window was June 15–August 18, 2026. Challenge hub · Track 1 · IJCAI competition directory

Competition research

Results and Retrospective Analysis of the CODS 2025 AssetOpsBench Challenge, a 2026 preprint, studies leaderboard behavior, hidden evaluation, scoring scales, participation, and submitted strategies. It complements the AAAI AssetOpsBench-Live system paper: one describes the platform; the other investigates what the competition actually measured.

Evaluation science: from benchmarks to deployment evidence

What does a benchmark score justify saying about an agent in an operational setting? This question connects benchmark development with measurement research and deployment practice.

Research foundation

Beyond Static Leaderboards: Predictive Validity for the Evaluation of LLM Agents, a June 2026 preprint, synthesizes fourteen parallel implementation studies and argues for evaluating whether rankings transfer beyond their original test conditions. It proposes testable predictive-validity criteria and explicitly notes that existing evidence is insufficient to confirm the position.

AAAI-27 Bridge · From Agent Benchmarks to Deployment Evidence

The Bridge website lists Bridging Evaluation Science and Deployment Practice for February 16–17, 2027, in Montréal, Canada. As of this overview's review date, this is an upcoming activity, with planned outputs.

The program brings benchmark builders and measurement researchers together with workflow owners, domain experts, and practitioners. Its industrial-maintenance case uses a configured agent in the AssetOpsBench simulated environment; a second case addresses software engineering. Participants will derive deployment criteria, inspect evaluation evidence, identify missing failure checks, and specify what a supervised pilot must still establish. Program and cases

Planned outputs include two worked case audits and a versioned protocol draft, building on PREP-Eval and mapping to existing benchmark assessment frameworks. The page lists December 1, 2026 for case or interest statements. Participation and dates

This gives evaluation science a visible place in the ecosystem: connecting scenarios, scoring, diagnostics, and operational claims. The competition retrospective supplies a concrete example of why that connection matters. CODS evaluation analysis
